## In a nutshell - Blues to Bop is the main music festival in Ticino with free concerts in the square - Ideal for border crossers looking for entertainment without access costs - Requires planning on transport and crossing times
## Key facts - **What**: Blues to Bop music festival with free concerts in the square - Where: Lugano, Canton Ticino, squares in the historic centre - Who: Jazz/blues music fans, borderers from Como, Lecco and Varese - When: Annual organization; 2026 details not yet specified - Why: Free cultural offer in Ticino for border families
Blues to Bop is the main music festival in Ticino dedicated to jazz and blues. In recent years, the event has consolidated a proposal of free concerts in the square, attracting not only residents of the Canton of Ticino, but also border workers who work or live in Switzerland. For those who daily cross the border between Italy and Ticino — from the municipalities of Como, Lecco, Varese to Menaggio — a Blues to Bop evening represents an opportunity for entertainment without access charges.
Free concerts in the square are the main advantage for border families. Unlike many European events, Blues to Bop maintains a completely free open-air model. This aspect is particularly appreciated by those who have to calculate each item of expenditure in evening trips from a work area in Ticino to border Italy, or vice versa.
However, ### How to Reach Lugano from the Border Region
Organizing a trip to Blues to Bop requires conscious choices regarding transportation, parking, and waiting times.
**From Como and Lecco**: The Chiasso pass is the most direct route for those coming from the Como province. The state road (then A2 highway) directly accesses Lugano in about 50-60 minutes in the absence of queues. During weekend concerts, the flow of vehicles entering and exiting the Ticino can create delays of 15-30 minutes. [Check real-time waiting times before departing](nav:border).
From Varese and province: The Gaggiolo or Brogeda pass is recommended. Both routes lead to the Lugano axis in 60-90 minutes depending on traffic. Brogeda represents a generally less congested alternative compared to Chiasso during weekends, although it is located slightly further north.
Public Transportation: For those who prefer not to drive, the Italian railway system (Trenitalia) connects Como to Lugano via Chiasso. Regional trains have an hourly frequency and the journey takes about 1 hour. Once in Lugano, the city's bus network reaches the squares where concerts take place. For frequent border crossers accustomed to Swiss public transportation, the Ticinese system is compatible and convenient.
### Parking and Waiting Costs
Lugano has paid parking lots in the city center with an average hourly rate of 1.00-1.50 EUR. For extended stays (2-3 hour concerts), the cost amounts to 2.00-4.50 EUR. Parking lots outside the historic center are available at a lower rate; the choice depends on walking availability.
Ensure that your car insurance policy covers circulation in Switzerland (border extension or specific frontier insurance). The insurance certificate must be on board during border crossing.
### Comprehensive Economic Considerations
The total cost of a evening trip for 2-3 people (A2 fuel, parking, coffee breaks) is approximately between 20-30 EUR. Add 5-10 EUR if you decide to have dinner after the concert. [Consult our calculator to estimate the costs of your trip](nav:calculator), including fuel, car maintenance, and parking.

For commuters crossing border crossings such as Chiasso, Brogeda or Gaggiolo, access to an efficient transport network is not just a convenience: it is a central element of the monthly budget. The Arcobaleno network offers different categories of subscriptions to adapt to different border profiles. Not all cross-border workers have the same mobility needs: those who work five days a week in the office have different needs from those who alternate teleworking with on-site days, and still different from those who rarely commute.
** Full subscriptions (unlimited use)**: They include an unlimited number of trips throughout the network during the validity period (daily, weekly, monthly, annual). They agree with the border worker who switches regularly and predictably. A monthly subscription, spread over about 20-22 working days, lowers the pro-travel cost at very competitive levels compared to the private car.
Time slot passes: Some fare solutions limit use to specific time slots (for example, valid only during morning/evening commute times). This category attracts commuters with fixed and predictable working hours, as the reduced fare compensates for less flexibility.
Combined subscriptions: Integrations with shared mobility systems (carpooling, bike-sharing) or discounted rates for couples or families allow further reductions. A household where both spouses work in Ticino can negotiate more advantageous solutions than buying two individual subscriptions.

Phase 1 — Needs Analysis: Estimate the number of weekly trips. If you average 10 round-trips (50 monthly trips), a monthly unlimited subscription is convenient. Calculate annual savings by dividing the monthly subscription cost by the average monthly trips: the cost per trip provides a benchmark. Compare it with the cost per kilometer of a private car (gasoline + fixed insurance and maintenance costs). Most commuters discover that switching to public transportation generates annual savings between CHF 2,000 and 4,000, depending on the distance and frequency of use.
This figure is not just a cost savings: it's time recovered (not spent in queues), reduced driving stress, and minimized environmental impact. Being a cross-border worker during pregnancy means coordinating two different healthcare systems. Those working in Switzerland with a G permit have the recognized right to opt for LAMal health insurance instead of Italian CMI. This is a choice that transforms access to prenatal check-ups, ultrasounds, and maternity management.
LAMal is mandatory Swiss health insurance. It operates through private funds at cantonal and national level. Deductibles vary: adults pay an annual deductible between CHF 300 and CHF 2500 according to the chosen policy. After reaching the deductible, the fund covers 90% of healthcare expenses up to a maximum of CHF 700 total annual deductible.
CMI is the Italian system managed by general practitioners and public hospitals. Coverage is free or with modulated contributions, but access times to services and the level of coordination with specialist facilities differ significantly from LAMal.
### Why the choice matters in pregnancy
During pregnancy, the number of healthcare check-ups increases: regular obstetric visits every two to three weeks, ultrasounds, blood tests, screening for gestational conditions. The speed of access to services and the quality of coverage become priorities. If you opt for LAMal, you immediately access Swiss facilities; if you remain with CMI, you coordinate with Italian hospitals with potentially longer waiting times.
Cross-border workers with a G permit have the discretion to choose: they can remain enrolled in CMI or opt for LAMal. This option is a right guaranteed by cross-border regulations and is not automatic. It requires a formal request to the chosen LAMal fund. The [insurance comparison calculator](nav:calculator) can help you evaluate options available in Ticino Canton. ### Which system to choose
There is no universal answer. The choice depends on where you live permanently, the network of medical contacts you have consolidated, and the quality of coverage you prioritize.
By choosing LAMal you gain access to Swiss hospitals with generally shorter waiting times for specialist visits. Hospitals in the Canton of Ticino are fully accessible by LAMal card. Prenatal check-ups will be coordinated with gynaecologists and hospitals operating according to Swiss protocols. Annual deductibles and costs are defined in advance, with no surprises.
By staying on CMI, you maintain direct connection with the Italian healthcare system where you reside. Your primary care doctors, the hospitals of the Italian province will become your points of reference. If you want access to Swiss specialists or facilities, you will face more complex procedures (authorisations, partial reimbursements) and costs not covered by the CMI.
### Practical scenario: pregnant woman with LAMal
A border worker who chooses LAMal in the fifth month of pregnancy contacts a cashier in the Canton of Ticino. He presents the G permit and the documentation of Italian residence. The cash register records it retroactively or from the following month, according to the administrative time (usually a few days). From that moment on, prenatal checks, ultrasounds, haematological examinations are covered according to the LAMal deductibles chosen. The process is straightforward, but requires clarity and timeliness. Here are the steps.
Step 1: Decide Which System to Prioritize
Reflect on your concrete situation: Where do you live stably during pregnancy and after childbirth? Where is your primary healthcare provider located? If you are already pregnant, which hospitals have you identified as your clinical reference? These questions guide your decision.
Step 2: Contact a LAMal Fund (if you Choose LAMal)
If you opt for LAMal, contact a fund in the Canton Ticino. Several operators exist (Helsana, Swica, CSS, Sanitas, and others). Ask for specific information about policies for cross-border workers, the range of deductibles available, and the registration procedure for G permit holders. The fund will explain the activation timeline.
**Step 3: Prepare Your Documentation**
You will need: your original G permit, your Italian residence document (anagrafe certificate or identity card), your employment contract in Switzerland, your Italian tax code. Some funds may require certification from your Swiss employer. Contact the fund directly for the exact list.
Step 4: Submit Your Registration Request
Send your documentation via email, physical counter, or the fund's online portal. Clearly specify that you are a cross-border worker with a G permit who intends to opt for LAMal. Indicate your desired start date (preferably within the first trimester of pregnancy). The fund will confirm your registration within a few days and provide the official activation date.
Step 5: Receive Your Card and Get Started
The fund will send you your LAMal card and official registration documentation. From the indicated date, you are covered by LAMal. Use your card at hospitals, clinics, and doctors in Ticino and Switzerland. Inform your medical contacts of your new registration.
### If You Remain on CMI
No request is necessary. You remain registered with the Italian system. Continue to use your Italian national health card with your primary care doctor and public hospitals.
### Timing and Administrative Deadlines
There is no strict legal deadline, but it is advisable to make your choice before becoming pregnant or within the first trimester of pregnancy. This allows your hospital contacts to coordinate widely before delivery and ensures continuity of care without interruptions. If you decide to switch after the fifth or sixth month, you will have little time to organize coordination between systems and confusion in clinical management could arise.

Those who work in Ticino with a G Permit pay mandatory contributions according to the Swiss system, managed by the AFC/ESTV and the cantonal offices. The employee pays about CHF 557 monthly between AVS (Old Age Insurance)/AI (Disability)/IPG (Lost Earnings Allowance): contribution 5.3%. The basis of calculation is the Swiss gross salary, not the Italian net salary.
AVS affiliation starts from the first day of work: there is no minimum income threshold to access. This continuity is crucial because the years of payment in Switzerland are added to the years of Italian residence in Italy at the INPS (National Social Security Institute), creating a global contribution account recognized by both countries for the purposes of old-age pension.

## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Startup Procedure: Concrete Steps
Before accepting a work assignment in Ticino, the cross-border worker must obtain the clearance (nulla osta) from the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration). The Ticino employer initiates the registration procedure with the SEM, attaching the employment contract, a specimen payslip, and copies of identity documents. The SEM communicates the Permit G number within approximately 5–10 working days; only after this notification can the contract begin. Working without SEM registration exposes both employee and employer to administrative penalties and retroactive exclusion from contributions.
### Annual Tax Procedure: Form 730 Declaration and Section CE
By April 30 of the year following the income (electronic submission by November 30 if through a tax advisor), the cross-border worker must file the tax return using form 730 (or the standard form if receiving other income). In section CE (dedicated to foreign employment income), the cross-border worker declares the Swiss gross amount, Swiss taxes withheld monthly at source, the applicable allowance (€7,500 or €10,000), the resulting Italian taxable income, and the tax credit equal to Swiss withholdings. The Revenue Agency calculates the income tax due and automatically offsets it against the credit, generating a refund if the resulting tax is less than the Swiss taxes already paid.
### Advantages and Economic Considerations
The G permit regime allows average tax savings of 30–40% compared to equivalent Italian employment, due to concentration of Swiss taxation (typically effective rates of 12–18% in Ticino, Valais, and Graubünden cantons) and the Italian tax credit. Swiss social contributions are slightly higher (10–13% total net) but cover a far more robust occupational pension plan (LPP) compared to the Italian second pillar, guaranteeing significantly higher annuities upon reaching retirement age. LAMal offers rapid access to specialist care without waiting lists for many conditions.
However, those residing in Italy and working in Switzerland bear fixed transport costs (fuel, vehicle wear, Ticino road tax, A2/A9 tolls), administrative expenses for cross-border tax filings (often handled by bilingual tax advisors, costing €80–120 annually), and currency risk CHF/EUR on compensation (Swiss income is subject to the monthly exchange rate in the 730 form). For those living in San Bartolomeo and working in Lugano or Mendrisio, commuting represents a daily burden of 40–80 minutes round-trip depending on border crossing traffic conditions.

Monitor the EUR/CHF exchange rate to estimate Italian net income and plan taxes

## In a nutshell - New Frontier Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 after signature on 23 December 2020 - New frontier workers: deductible €10,000 per year; old frontier workers: exemption €7,500 with transition until 2033 - Tax at source withheld ONLY in Switzerland; LAMal mandatory with option right for G border workers
## Key facts - **What**: New tax regime for Italy-Ticino border workers with new deductibles and rates - When: Effective from 1 January 2024 (Italian ratification: Law 83 of 13 June 2023) - Where: Canton Ticino (Switzerland) and Venegono Superiore (province of Varese, Italy) - Who: Frontier workers residing in Italy and working in Switzerland - Excess amount: €10,000 per year for new frontier workers; €7,500 for old frontier workers before 17 July 2023
Those who reside in Venegono Superiore and choose to work in Ticino enter a deeply renewed regulatory framework. The New Frontier Agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and entered into force on 1 January 2024, has transformed the taxation and contribution rules for thousands of Italian commuters who cross the Swiss border daily towards the Canton of Ticino. Law 83 of 13 June 2023 ratified the commitments signed in Italy, making the new regime definitive and applicable to all new border workers from January 2024 onwards.
The choice to live in Italy, where the cost of living remains lower, and to work in Switzerland, where wages are structurally The tax and contribution structure for a border worker who lives in Venice and works in Ticino is divided into three levels: Swiss source tax, social contributions, and health insurance.
### Tax at source and contributions: the actual weight of the paycheck
The following are withheld from the gross amount agreed with the Ticino employer, before the net payment to the border agent: - **AVS/AI/IPG**: 5.3% to be paid by the employee - AD/AC (unemployment insurance and salary continuation): 1.1% (capped at CHF 148,200 annual salary) - LAINF (accident insurance): 0.7-1.5%, generally borne by the employer - LPP (occupational pension): 7–18% depending on the age group (from 25th year onwards)
These amounts reduce the gross declared for Swiss federal tax purposes. However, the Ticino employer does not withhold any "source tax" (so-called "withholding tax") because the border worker, although resident in Italy, is subject to the border regime G, which provides for taxation in the canton where he works. The calculation of the pillowcase and cantonal tax therefore takes place on the income already reduced by social contributions, and Ticino applies its own progressive tax rates, which vary with the annual net income.
In Italy, the border worker records Swiss income and benefits from the tax credit for taxes already paid in Switzerland. Italian income tax has progressive rates: 23% up to

For the cross-border worker who decides to live in Venegono Superiore and work in Ticino, the concrete steps to take follow a logical sequence: obtain the G permit, register with Swiss authorities, notify income to the Italian INPS, and manage annual tax filing obligations.
### Phase 1: Registration and G Permit
The first step is registration with the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration), obtaining the G permit (cross-border worker). This must be requested before starting work in Ticino: the employer provides a "letter of employment confirmation" that the cross-border worker presents to the Italian consulate or directly to the cantonal migration office. The G permit is tied to the employer: if you change companies, the permit must be updated. Its validity is 5 years, renewable.
### Phase 2: AVS Registration, Pension, and LAMal
Once the permit is obtained, the employer automatically registers the worker with the AVS (Compensation Office for Swiss Social Insurance), the company's LPP fund, and the Italian INPS is automatically notified via tax declarations. For LAMal, the cross-border worker receives a communication from the Ticino Canton (DSS, Department of Health) with information on approved insurance funds and the deadline (generally 30 days) to exercise the right of choice. If choosing Swiss LAMal, proceed with registration at the selected company; if maintaining Italian INPS, communicate the choice via the appropriate form and keep the documentation.
### Phase 3: Annual Tax Declaration and Refunds
Every year by September 30, the cross-border worker completes the Unico tax declaration (formerly 730) at the Italian Tax Agency (office or CAF), attaching certificates of Swiss income and taxes paid in Switzerland. In section CE, report foreign taxes paid and obtain the calculation of the tax credit. If the credit exceeds the IRPEF owed, a refund is issued that goes to the indicated bank account. This process became even more transparent from 2024 thanks to the new agreement, which standardized Swiss income certificates (SERP-RIV form) and coordinated timelines between Switzerland and Italy.
### Critical Deadlines and Essential Documents
- Within 30 days of hiring: AVS registration with employer - **Within 30 days of hiring**: LAMal right of choice notification (if G permit holder) - By June 30 of the following year: receipt of income certificate (annual pay statement) from Swiss employer - By September 30: submission of Unico tax declaration with attached Swiss certificates - November–December: possible modification of LAMal option for following year
Documents to keep: G permit (original), employment contract, annual Swiss income certificates, LAMal contract or INPS documentation, contribution payment receipts (sent by employer in pay statement), signed Unico declarations and transmission receipts.

## In Brief - New Frontier Agreement in force from January 1, 2024 (Italian ratification: Law 83/2023) - Tax exemptions: CHF 7,500 for historical frontiers, CHF 10,000 for new ones (from July 17, 2023) - Withholding tax: ONLY in Switzerland, credit for tax recognized in Italy - Federal deductions: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3%, AD/AC 1.1%, LAINF 0.7–1.5%
## Key Facts - **What**: Tax and pension regime for frontiers with Italy-Ticino G Permit - When: In force from January 1, 2024 - Where: Frontiers from Italian municipalities (Nesso and Lario area) to Ticino - Who: Holders of G Permit authorized by SEM - Historical exemption: CHF 7,500 per year (transitional regime 2024–2033) - New exemption: CHF 10,000 per year (frontiers from July 17, 2023) - Withholding tax: 5.3% AVS/AI/IPG withheld by the Swiss employer - Double taxation convention: December 9, 1976
Living in Nesso, a picturesque municipality on the Lombardy side of Lake Lario, and commuting daily to Ticino for work has become a consolidated reality for thousands of frontiers. The regulatory framework governing this condition has been renewed with the New Frontier Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, and entered into force on January 1, 2024 through Italian ratification via Law 83 of June 13, 2023.
The foundation of your frontier situation is the G Permit (authorization for cross-border work). With this document, the Swiss employer applies a withholding tax automatically – a direct deduction calculated on the paycheck according to the Ticino federal rates. Crucial point: this withholding occurs exclusively in Switzerland, not in Italy. Italy, aware of this taxation, recognizes the principle of the Italy-Switzerland Double Taxation Convention (signed on December 9, 1976) and prevents double taxation through the tax credit, which is declared in the annual income tax return in Italy (model 730, CE section) by attaching the certificates of Swiss withholding.
The main novelty of the New Agreement concerns frontier tax exemptions. If you were already a frontier before July 17, 2023, you are entitled to a CHF 7,500 per year exemption on employment income. This benefit is temporary: it integrates a transitional regime 2024–2033, after which it will be reduced progressively. If you are a new frontier (from July 17, 2023), the exemption is more generous: CHF 10,000 per year. This protection allows you to operate a portion of income without taxation in Italy, significantly reducing the IRPEF tax burden.
### Contributions and deductions in the paycheck
As a dependent in Switzerland, your gross salary is subject to mandatory federal deductions. The AVS/AI/IPG (Old Age, Disability, Maternity Insurance) involves a 5.3% withdrawal. Contributions against unemployment (AD/AC) amount to 1.1% up to a maximum of CHF 148,200 per year. The accident insurance (LAINF) varies from 0.7% to 1.5%. The second pillar (LPP, professional pension) is mandatory from the age of 25: the employer pays 7%–18% of the gross salary depending on the age class, credited entirely to your pension account.
These deductions affect the net paycheck. For a precise simulation of how much you will actually earn month by month, [use the frontier paycheck calculator](nav:calculator). To understand the Italian-Swiss bilateral fiscal structure is essential for planning your move to Nesso. The taxation of foreign income follows a precise architecture established by the 1976 Convention and strengthened by the 2024 New Agreement.

It is not automatic; you choose whether to cover in Switzerland or keep the Italian system (public SSN). If you opt for the Swiss LAMal, take out a policy at a recognized sickness fund (Assura, CSS, Helsana, Visana, etc.). The deductibles (deductibles) can be parameterized: - Adults: CHF 300-2,500 per year (choose at the time of subscription) - Higher the deductible, lower the monthly premium - After deductible, you pay 10% of the expenses up to the maximum, then the cash pays 100% It is not a "health tax"; it is a mutual protection system with total coverage after deductible. Alternative: keep the Italian SSN (free for residents) and add a Swiss private supplementary policy for benefits not covered by the Italian SSN (full dentistry, eye care, psychotherapy, etc.). Many border workers choose this solution to save on the LAMal premium while having extra coverage. Critical deadline: the choice must be made within 3 months of the first employment relationship in Switzerland. After the deadline, you pay double the prize if you want to sign up late. # ## AVS: on No cantonal tax Ticino, being border. 5. Annual declaration (May following year) Fill in form 730 (via CAF) or PF Income. In the EC framework, it declares Swiss gross income, withholdings, border exemption (€7,500 or €10,000), tax credit. Those who decide to move to Colonno to work in Ticino must complete a series of administrative steps. Here is a simplified procedure.
### Phase 1: Before Departure
1. Verify with the employer: communicate the intention to move to Colonno and verify that the employer is available to request a G permit (frontalier daily). Not all employers cooperate with Swiss authorities for this type of authorization.
2. **Residence information**: contact the Comune of Colonno for information on registering residence for Swiss citizens (if CH citizen) or for EU citizens. It is also possible to verify with the Como Questura.

- The typical process takes 4-6 weeks from the employer's request.
### Phase 3: Fiscal Registration in Italy
- Register with the Italian Revenue Agency with the new residence in Colonno. It is necessary to communicate the tax code and the INPS registration number.

Choose between the two available options for the G frontaliere:
- LAMal Swiss: franchise from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 (depending on age and canton), monthly premiums from CHF 150-300. Offers complete coverage according to Swiss standards.
- Italian insurance (INPS or SSN): less expensive, but requires registration with the Italian Revenue Agency. It is useful to verify with the employer if it is acceptable.
### Phase 5: First Year and Annual Management
- Maintain the Swiss documentation (contract, pay slips, CU-ELF certification from the source) for the annual tax returns.
- Complete the income tax return in Italy every year, indicating in the CE box the income from foreign work (Switzerland) and the taxes withheld at source.
- Verify with an Italian accountant if there are opportunities for annual tax returns due to the recognized tax credit.

In addition, a tool for verifying [annual tax returns](nav:ristorni) allows you to estimate the amount recoverable thanks to the recognized tax credit by the Italian tax authorities.
### Final Considerations: Does it Really Pay to Move?
Living in Colonno and working in Ticino is a practical and, for many, economically advantageous choice. The New Frontalieri Agreement in force from January 1, 2024 has improved the fiscal conditions compared to the past, especially for old frontiersmen who benefit from the exemption of €7,500. The travel times from Colonno to the Ticino poles (via Brogeda, Chiasso or Gaggiolo) are sustainable for daily commuting. The administrative procedure remains complex: it is strongly recommended to entrust an Italian professional with the fiscal aspect and a Ticinese cantonal consultant with the G permit. The time invested in this initial preparation is quickly recovered thanks to the economic benefits of Italian residence and the fiscal benefits of the bilateral agreement.

AVS (old-age and survivors' insurance) and AI (disability insurance) are mandatory: the deduction is 5.3% of the gross salary for the employee. AD (unemployment insurance) covers the risk of job loss with an additional 1.1% deduction up to the annual ceiling (CHF 148,200). LAINF (occupational accident insurance) is the employer's responsibility and covers work-related incidents. Finally, LPP (professional pension insurance / second pillar) varies between 7% and 18% of the salary depending on the age class (obligatory from the 25th birthday) and the company's pension plan. On the Italian side, income from Switzerland is declared through the model 730 or RdC (category income), with the application of the €10,000 exemption for new cross-border workers and the deduction of the tax credit for withholding taxes already paid to the Canton. INPS and the Revenue Agency manage, respectively, the verification of Italian social security contributions (minimum integration) and the correct application of the 2024 Border Workers Agreement. ### Choosing Health Insurance Health insurance is a crucial step. In Switzerland, enrollment in a LAMal (Federal Law on Health Insurance) is mandatory: it is coverage with a deductible (from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 for adults) and variable monthly premiums according to the company and risk. Cross-border workers have the right to choose: they can opt to remain enrolled in the Italian healthcare system (SSN + private supplementary insurance) or switch to Swiss LAMal. The choice affects access to services, delivery times, direct costs, and the network of usable facilities. To proceed effectively, it is advisable to: - Request from the Swiss employer all necessary documentation for registration with federal authorities (employment declaration, company data, name of the SUVA intermediary if present). - Open a bank account with a bank operating in both countries (CHF and EUR) to simplify payroll and recurring payment management. - Evaluate the convenience between Swiss LAMal and Italian supplementary insurance with the support of an intermediary familiar with both systems. - Verify with the Italian municipality of residence the registration as a foreign resident and communication with the Guardia di Finanza for compliance with declarative obligations. - Consult the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to simulate the net paycheck and verify the impact of the €10,000 exemption on the annual declaration. Moving as a cross-border worker from Bene Lario to Ticino is an economically advantageous choice for many, but it requires careful planning regarding taxes, permits, social security, and healthcare. Having clear documentation from the start and following the scheduled administrative timelines significantly reduces stress and costs during the transition.

item.title: Moving to Vertemate from border crossing Ticino
item.description: Living in Vertemate with Minoprio and working in Switzerland: advantages of the new 2024 agreement with €10,000 deductible, taxation, G permit and administrative checklist.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - New free-at-frontier agreement from 1 January 2024 with €10,000 deductible for new frontier workers - Tax at source withheld only in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy avoids double taxation - Permit G mandatory; procedure with SEM within 8 working days from the certificate of residence
## Key facts - **What**: New border tax agreement Ticino-Italy - When: Signed December 23, 2020, effective January 1, 2024 - Where: Italy-Switzerland Frontier (Can. Ticino prevalente) - Ratification Italy: Law 83 of 13 June 2023 - New border excess: €10,000 per year - Old border deductible: €7,500 per year (transitional 2024–2033)
With the entry into force of the new Franco-frontier agreement on 1 January 2024, Ticino border workers residing in Italy benefit from a significantly renewed tax regime. Vertemate with Minoprio, in the province of Como, is one of the areas that attract those who decide to maintain employment in Switzerland by residing in Lombardy. The choice of transfer entails tangible advantages but also administrative responsibilities that go beyond the simple housing decision.
The agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and made operational on 1 January 2024, introduces exemptions from Italian taxation on labour income up to a defined threshold. Border workers who were already classified as such before 17 July 2023 benefit from a deductible of €7,500 per year until 2033, ### Tax and social security aspects for the border worker
The tax framework of a border worker resident in Italy is complex and structured on several levels. For the purposes of the Swiss Confederation, the border worker contributes to the AVS (Old Age and Survivors Insurance), the AI (Invalidity Insurance) and the IPG (Maternity Allowance) with a total rate of 5.3% borne by the employee. In addition, it pays unemployment (AD) and insolvency (AC) insurance contributions at a rate of 1.1%, as well as LAINF contributions (0.7–1.5% for accidents). If you are part of an occupational pension plan (LPP, second pillar), the deduction varies between 7% and 18% depending on the age group.
On the Italian side, the border crossing is subject to personal income tax with progressive rates: 23% up to €28,000, 35% from €28,001 to €50,000, and 43% over €50,000. However, the excess introduced by the 2024 agreement significantly mitigates this exposure. To give an example: a new frontier worker with an annual gross income of €35,000 gross in Switzerland, benefiting from the deductible of €10,000, would have the Italian tax base reduced to €25,000, subject to the 23% IRPEF rate.
A key aspect: the frontier worker continues to benefit from the Swiss pension system without any duplication of contributions. AVS/AI payments are accredited by the Swiss employer directly, and the border worker must not contribute further to the Italian INPS
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Before Transfer: Essential Administrative Requirements
Anyone deciding to move to Vertemate with Minoprio as a frontier worker must complete a series of administrative procedures in logical sequence. First, verify that your employment contract in Switzerland is valid and was signed before the G permit application: this is a non-negotiable preliminary requirement.
In parallel, register as a resident in Vertemate at the Municipal Registry Office. Once registration is complete, obtain your Italian certificate of residence, an essential document for the frontier permit application. Submit your G permit application to the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) of the Canton of Ticino within 8 working days from the date the certificate is issued. You will attach the valid Swiss employment contract, the Italian certificate of residence, and the documentation required by the Ticino cantonal authorities.
Once you obtain the permit, inform the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia Entrate) of your new status as a frontier worker via a pre-filled return or Form 730, specifically indicating your G frontier worker status. In parallel, update your status with the competent federal office (SECO or coordination with BFS for correct management of AVS/AI/IPG contributions) so that Swiss contributions are tracked correctly.
### Critical Deadlines and Annual Taxation
Once resident in Vertemate, the frontier worker must file two coordinated tax returns. In Italy, the income tax return (Form 730 or Form 4) must be filed by September 30 of the year following the tax year. In Section CE of the Italian return, a tax credit is reported to prevent double taxation on amounts subject to Swiss tax. In Switzerland, the cantonal tax return (D-CA2 or equivalent for frontier workers) must be filed with the Ticino Cantonal Tax Administration by the established deadline (generally in summer, to be verified annually).
The first year of transfer is critical: timely and accurate communication to both tax systems (Italy and Switzerland) significantly reduces the risk of penalties, official corrections, or administrative misunderstandings. Many frontier workers entrust this coordination to a tax consultant specializing in cross-border taxation.
### Practical Tools for Planning
Frontaliere Ticino provides [a net salary calculator](nav:calculator) that allows you to concretely evaluate the impact of the €10'000 (or €7'500) exemption and Swiss withholding tax on your monthly and annual pay. It is recommended to simulate different income scenarios before the transfer to get a realistic estimate of your net take-home pay. For more details on G permit administrative procedures and specific cantonal authority contacts, consult the [Frontier Permits](nav:permits) section. If you wish to assess the cost of living differential between Vertemate and Ticino, the [Cost of Living Comparator](nav:cost-of-living) allows detailed comparisons of rent, utilities, groceries, and services.

item.title: Living in Faggeto Lario and working in Ticino
item.description: From 1 January 2024, the New Frontier Agreement changes the taxation. Discover Permit G, tax at source, AVS and LAMal for those who reside in Faggeto Lario and work in Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In Brief - From January 1, 2024, New Agreement: exemption of €7,500 (old border workers) or €10,000 (new) - Source tax in Switzerland; Italy credit for CE framework (no double taxation) - G permit mandatory; LAMal optional with CHF 300–2,500 fees - AVS/AI contributions 5.3%, AD 1.1%, LAINF 0.7–1.5%, LPP 7–18% for age range
## Key Facts - **What**: Living in Faggeto Lario (Como) and working as a border worker in Ticino - When: January 1, 2024 (effective date of New Border Workers Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020) - Where: Como-Ticino border, Brogeda, Gaggiolo, Chiasso - Who: Italian residents with G permit - Amount: Exemption of €7,500 (old border workers, before July 17, 2023) or €10,000 (new); transitional regime 2024–2033 - Rates: AVS/AI 5.3% dependent; AD/AC 1.1% (CHF 148,200 cap); LAINF 0.7–1.5%; LPP 7–18% for age range from 25
Faggeto Lario, an Italian border town on Lake Como, offers a strategic location for those working in Ticino as border workers. From January 1, 2024, the New Border Workers Agreement (signed on December 23, 2020 and ratified in Italy with law 83/2023) introduces new rules on taxation that modify the economic balance of those residing in Italy and earning in Switzerland.
The fiscal pillar of the border worker is the source tax: applied exclusively in Switzerland on income from work, while Italy applies a tax credit through the model 730 (CE framework) to avoid double taxation. This means that the income is taxed only once — in Switzerland — and the border worker recovers the amount paid as withholding in Italian tax declaration, theoretically zeroing out the Italian tax on foreign income.
The New Agreement distinguishes two categories. Old border workers (already so before July 17, 2023) enjoy an exemption of €7,500 per year, with a transitional regime until 2033. New border workers (from July 17, 2023 onwards) have a €10,000 annual exemption. These thresholds reduce the taxable base in Switzerland for those residing in Italy, alleviating the tax burden compared to the past and simplifying the calculation of withholding taxes.
### G permit and bilateral legislation To work legally in Ticino, a G permit (border worker) is required, which authorizes daily or periodic commuting from Italian residence to Swiss workplace without the obligation to transfer residence. The G permit is governed by the Convention signed on December 9, 1976 between Italy and Switzerland, which entered into force on January 1, 1977. Switzerland is not a member of the European Union, so the legislation on border workers depends entirely on specific bilateral agreements.
The G permit application is presented to the competent cantonal office (Migration Section, SEM) in coordination with the Italian municipality of residence. The typical validity is annual or multi-annual (up to 5 years), renewable. In addition to income taxes, the border worker pays AVS/AI contributions (5.3% dependent), AD/AC (1.1% with CHF 148,200 cap), LAINF (0.7–1.5% accident insurance) and LPP (company pension fund: 7–18% according to age range, from 25 years on). ### Health Insurance and LAMal Option
The border worker with a G permit has the right to opt for Swiss health insurance (LAMal): they are not obliged to submit to the Swiss system if they are covered by the Italian National Health Service. Many border workers choose to maintain Italian assistance (INPS/ASL) and subscribe to private supplementary insurance policies to fill gaps in Swiss healthcare.
Those who decide to join LAMal pay an annual deductible for adults ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2500, depending on the product chosen, the health insurance company (CS, Helsana, Sympany, Concordia), and the individual's personal risk class. LAMal covers medical services in Switzerland and, under certain limits defined by bilateral agreements, also emergency hospitalizations and treatments in Italy.
The choice between LAMal Swiss and SSN Italian depends on the cost/benefit calculation. LAMal is considered more expensive than Italian healthcare, but it offers a high-standard hospital network and shorter waiting times for some specialist services. The border worker must evaluate the frequency of hospital services, the quality of local services in Como/Faggeto Lario, and private supplementary insurance premiums to fill any gaps.
### Net Salary Scenario: a Hypothetical Example
Consider a border worker resident in Faggeto Lario with a permanent contract in Ticino and a gross income of CHF 80,000 per year. After applying Swiss contributions and taxes:
- AVS/AI: 5.3% = CHF 4,240 - AD/AC: 1.1% = CHF 880 - LAINF (medium): 1.0% = CHF 800 - LPP (7% for the 25-34 age group): CHF 5,600 - Source tax (federal and cantonal Ticino, variable): approximately CHF 12,000-15,000
The estimated net income is between CHF 56,000 and CHF 60,000 per year, after Swiss deductions. In Italy, the border worker declares their worldwide income (CHF 80,000 converted to EUR at the annual average exchange rate) and applies the tax credit for the Swiss deductions made in the model 730 (CE frame). The Italian IRPEF, with tax rates ranging from 23% (income up to €28,000) to 43% (over €50,000), is calculated on the declared total income, but the foreign tax credit theoretically reduces the final Italian tax, eliminating double taxation.
The New Agreement 2024 simplifies this mechanism: the €7,500 exemption (old border workers) or €10,000 (new) reduces the Swiss taxable income, resulting in a lower initial source tax and easing both Swiss and Italian tax administration. For a border worker with a gross income of CHF 80,000, the €10,000 exemption (if new) would lower the Swiss taxable income to CHF 70,000, proportionally reducing the federal and cantonal tax.
### INPS Italian Contributions and Overlapping
A critical aspect is the overlap between Swiss AVS/LPP contributions and Italian INPS contributions. The Italian resident border worker remains subject to INPS contributions on Italian income (if they have activities in Italy) and Italian pension contribution discipline. However, the Italy-Switzerland Convention provides coordination rules: Swiss AVS contributions can be coordinated with Italian pension rights to avoid duplicate contributions.
The [salary calculator](nav:calculator) on the website facilitates the estimation of the net monthly salary with all 2024 border worker taxes applied. It is recommended to simulate the monthly salary before signing a Swiss contract to understand the actual net income after deductions and contributions.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Checklist: what to check before moving to Faggeto Lario
If you consider moving your residence to Faggeto Lario to work as a border worker in Ticino, an organized procedure simplifies the bureaucratic steps and avoids delays in starting work.
Step 1: Change of residence and request for Permit G
Contact the municipality of Faggeto Lario for registration of residence. At the same time, submit the application for [Permit G](nav:permits) to the competent Swiss cantonal office (Migration Section, SEM, or migration office of the canton of Ticino). Required documents: valid passport or identity card, Swiss employment contract signed, Italian residence certificate. Permit G is issued on average within 4–8 weeks. Keep a copy: it will be needed for bank account openings, AVS enrollments, and tax declarations.
Step 2: LAMal and health insurance
Decide whether to join the Swiss LAMal or maintain the Italian SSN. If you choose LAMal, enroll with a Swiss health insurance company (Concordia, CS, Helsana, Sympany) within 3 months of your first day of employment in Switzerland. If you remain with the Italian SSN, check with the competent ASL for reciprocal coverage for services received in Switzerland and consult the Agenzia Entrate website for details on protective territorial extension.
Step 3: Enrollment in AVS/AI and opening of contributory account
The Swiss employer automatically enrolls the border worker in AVS (Old Age and Survivors Insurance) on the first day of work. You will receive a 16-digit AVS number, communicated via post or email. Keep the documentation: AVS payment certificates are essential for the annual Italian tax declaration and for tracking future Swiss pension rights.
Step 4: Italian tax declaration and CE form of the 730
Every year, by May 31, complete the model 730 at the Agenzia Entrate (online via portal, or through CAF - Fiscal Assistance Office). In the CE form, declare the income earned in Switzerland (gross, converted to EUR) and the withholding taxes paid in Switzerland. Attach Swiss certificates of payment (Bulletin de Salaire, bank statements, or downloadable via online banking from the Swiss bank or SECO portal). The Agenzia Entrate automatically calculates the tax credit: compare the Italian IRPEF tax on the declared income with the taxes already paid in Switzerland, and return or offset the difference.
Step 5: Check for updates on the New Agreement 2024
Periodically consult the Agenzia Entrate and MEF (Ministry of Economy and Finance) websites for details on the new border worker regulations. Tax deadlines, exemptions, transitional regime, and withholding tax rates may be subject to annual updates. Subscribe to official mailing lists or follow Agenzia Entrate press releases on border worker taxation to avoid missing relevant normative changes.
Step 6: Contacts and practical resources
- Permit G: SEM/Migration Section, canton of Ticino, seco.admin.ch - AVS and Swiss contributions: employer and SECO portal - Italian taxes: Agenzia Entrate (agenziaentrate.gov.it), section 'Border workers and foreign residents' - Italy-CH Convention: Agenzia Entrate, technical publications
### Next steps: tools and net income calculation
Use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) on the website to simulate the net salary with the 2024 border worker rates. Find out about the available LAMal and health insurance options and verify the [detailed information on Permit G and release procedure](nav:permits). If you want to compare the [cost of living between Faggeto Lario and the Ticino areas where you will work](nav:cost-of-living), consult the comparative guide.

item.title: Living in Capiago Intimiano, working in Ticino
item.description: Practical guide for border workers: location, commuting times, taxation, living costs and checklist before transfer.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Capiago Intimiano is less than 15 km from the Brogeda border crossing, the nearest border to southern Ticino - Source tax withheld ONLY in Switzerland; Italy applies IRPEF with tax credit - New Border Commuters Agreement in force from January 1, 2024: exemptions of €10'000 (new) or €7'500 (established commuters) - Lower cost of living compared to Ticino is the main economic advantage
## Key facts - **What**: living in the Italian municipality of Capiago Intimiano and working in Canton Ticino as a border commuter with permit G - Where: Capiago Intimiano (province of Como, Lombardy), distance from Brogeda/Chiasso border crossings 10–20 km - Who: border commuters with employment income in Switzerland - When: current regulations have been in force since January 1, 2024 (New Border Commuters Agreement) - Fiscal treatment: source tax in Switzerland (5.3% AVS/AI/IPG employee + cantonal contributions), Italian IRPEF with section CE
### Geographic location and logistics Capiago Intimiano is located in the province of Como, in Lombardy, just a few kilometers from the Ticino border. The Brogeda border crossing, the southernmost border passage from Ticino to Lombardy, is the natural crossing point for those living in Capiago and working in southern Ticino municipalities such as Mendrisio, Chiasso, or in the Ceresio area. Chiasso, the region's main border crossing, also remains accessible within reasonable times, making Capiago Intimiano a logistically viable choice for border commuters working in various economic sectors of Canton Ticino, from Lugano to Bellinzona down to smaller centers.
The choice to live in Capiago rather than relocate to Ticino has traditionally been attractive to border commuters for one primary economic reason: the cost of living in Lombardy is lower than that of Switzerland. Real estate, groceries, services, and utilities cost less compared to Ticino, allowing the border commuter to gain a financial advantage while maintaining access to the Ticino labor market, where salaries are on average higher than in the bordering Italian territory.
It is essential, however, to understand that the relocation entails obtaining a [permit G](nav:permits) (border commuter), which is issued and administered by the Ticino cantonal authorities and allows continuous work in Switzerland with residence in Italy. The required documentation and processing times vary, but obtaining the permit is an indispensable administrative prerequisite. ### Taxation: double taxation and the new 2024 agreement
Among the most delicate issues for the border worker who lives in Capiago Intimiano and works in Ticino is the management of double taxation. The Convention between Italy and Switzerland to avoid double taxation (signed on 9 December 1976) provides that the tax at source is withheld exclusively in Switzerland by the employer. This withholding covers AVS/AI/IPG (5.3% for the employee), Ticino cantonal contributions and insurance. Italy does not apply further direct taxation on the same source of income, but integrates with the IRPEF in the EC framework of the tax return (form 730), where the border worker can benefit from a tax credit equal to the taxes paid in Switzerland.
The New Frontier Agreement, which entered into force on 1 January 2024, introduced income exemptions: frontier workers who were already exempt before 17 July 2023 (old frontier workers) benefit from an exemption of €7,500 per year until 31 December 2033, while new frontier workers enjoy an exemption of €10,000. These deductibles reduce the Italian tax base and, consequently, the overall tax burden.
### Contributions and health insurance
All employee income is subject to mandatory Swiss contributions: AVS (old age), AI (disability), IPG (maternity allowance), as well as unemployment (AD/AC) and accident insurance (LAINF).
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Practical Checklist: Before Moving to Capiago Intimiano
Migration from a Ticino region to Capiago Intimiano requires a sequence of administrative obligations. The first step is to obtain a G permit from the competent cantonal authority (usually the Department of Health and Social Services — DSS — or the cantonal immigration office). A work contract signed by a Ticino company and proof of stable housing in Capiago Intimiano are required. Timelines vary, but the procedure can take several weeks.
Simultaneously, it is essential to register with the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) competent for the municipality of Capiago in order to communicate your change of residence and G permit number. The INPS must be informed of the start of cross-border work activity in Switzerland to register foreign contributions. Then you must choose a health insurance regime: whether to remain in the Italian NHS or subscribe to a Swiss LAMal with enrollment in a Ticino health insurance fund.
Another crucial aspect is opening a bank account with a Ticino bank (or one operating in Switzerland) to receive your paycheck in Swiss francs. Swiss banks, particularly those active at the cantonal level (Banca Cantonale Ticinese, UBS, Credit Suisse and others), accept Italian cross-border workers subject to anti-money laundering compliance checks. It is advisable to have the following documentation: G permit, work contract, Italian residence certificate, identity document.
### Tax Return Declaration and Annual Timeline
Every year by May 31st (ordinary deadline for Form 730) the cross-border worker must file an Italian tax return, reporting income from work declared by Switzerland, taxes withheld at source, amounts from any Ticino tax refunds and the application of tax credits. If you own real estate in Italy, these must be included according to ordinary taxation. If you purchased or changed your residence during the year, it is essential to communicate this promptly to the Revenue Agency to avoid discrepancies in automated audits.
### Commuting Costs and Final Economic Balance
Although the cost of living in Capiago is lower, cross-border workers must account for recurring commuting costs: the Swiss vehicle tax (vignette), motorway tolls (A2, A9 if using Lombardy connections), fuel and vehicle maintenance. Depending on the exact workplace in Ticino (Mendrisio, Lugano, Bellinzona, Locarno), the daily commute varies from 20 to 100 km, impacting fuel consumption. Some Ticino companies offer transportation benefits or commuting subsidies, reducing individual burden.
One final consideration: if the choice to live in Capiago is driven by the economic advantage over Ticino, it is useful to make a precise simulation of total costs (fiscal + commuting + real estate) versus moving to Ticino itself. [Use the tax calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate the Swiss withholding tax and net income received, comparing it with the hypothetical scenario of a Ticino residence. Based on the data, the choice will become more informed.

item.title: Living in Albese with Cassano and working in Ticino
item.description: Albese with Cassano is a convenient choice for Ticino border crossers: cost of living, G permit, 2024 taxes and border crossings illustrated in detail.
item.content:encoded:
## In Brief - Albese con Cassano is a municipality in the province of Como, Intelvi Valley, Ticino border - New frontier agreement in force from January 1, 2024 - Source tax withheld only in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy - G permit required; €10,000 exemption (new frontiersmen)
## Key Facts - **What**: Declare dependent income in Switzerland as a frontier resident in Como - When: New agreement from January 1, 2024 - Where: Ticino-Como border (Brogeda, Chiasso, Gaggiolo, Ponte Tresa passes) - Who: Frontiersmen with G permit, employees in Ticino, residents in Italy - Amount: €10,000 annual exemption (new frontiersmen); €7,500 exemption (old frontiersmen until 2033)
Albese con Cassano, a small municipality in the province of Como in Lombardy, attracts an increasing number of frontiersmen who choose to live a few kilometers from the Ticino border due to cost of living and proximity to work. The decision to move from one Italian region to a border location is not only a geographical issue: it has significant implications in terms of taxation, social security, and acquired rights on the transfrontier labor front.
With the entry into force of the new frontier agreement on January 1, 2024 (signed on December 23, 2020 and ratified in Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023), the terms of the Italian-Swiss Convention of December 9, 1976 have been modified, which directly affect the calculation of taxes on income from work and the social security treatment of those living in Como and working in Switzerland.
### Why choose the Como-Ticino border
The province of Como, particularly the municipalities of the Intelvi Valley such as Albese con Cassano, represents a balanced solution for those who want to work in the Swiss cantons (especially Ticino) while reducing housing costs. The Italian-Swiss economic dualism offers frontiersmen a logistical advantage: the short daily commute is compensated by a higher purchasing power in the Comasco Valley compared to Ticinese municipalities of similar size. Rents, food and services remain generally less expensive in the province of Como, even if they are nearby the border.
The main passes for those residing in Albese are Brogeda (for the Intelvi Valley), Chiasso (via A2), Gaggiolo (via SP San Fedele-Cassano) and Ponte Tresa (western side). Each pass has variable access conditions and waiting times depending on the time, season and traffic events; the choice depends on the workplace in Ticino (Lugano, Bellinzona, Locarno, Mendrisio).
### The frontier worker permit (G permit)
Frontiersmen who work in Ticino and reside in Albese con Cassano need a G permit, issued by the Italian authorities for the right to perform a subordinate activity in Switzerland. The G permit is subject to the signing of an employment contract with a Ticinese employer and represents the fundamental document for crossing the border daily. It is a personal document that cannot be transferred, issued by the Questura or Prefecture of Como, and has multi-year validity (usually 5-10 years) provided the employment relationship in Switzerland is maintained. Read the [guide to frontier worker permits (nav:permits)](nav:permits) for details on the application. ## Cross-Border Taxation in the 2024-2033 Regime
The new cross-border agreement modifies the tax regime for individuals living in Italy and working in Switzerland. Income tax withheld by the Swiss employer is based solely on the federal, cantonal, and municipal tax rates of Ticino. Italy does not apply a parallel source tax: the risk of double taxation is managed through the mechanism of tax credit in the model 730, section CE.
This means that as a cross-border resident in Como, you receive a net Swiss salary (with Swiss taxes deducted) and subsequently declare the gross income in Italy, benefiting from the Swiss tax credit to offset the Italian tax on the same taxable base.
### Transitional Regime: Old and New Cross-Border Residents
The new agreement distinguishes between two categories:
**Old Cross-Border Residents** (residing in Italy before July 17, 2023): benefit from an exemption of €7,500 per year on the Italian portion of income, valid from 2024 to 2033. This means that the income subject to Italian taxation is reduced by €7,500.
New Cross-Border Residents (residing in Italy from July 17, 2023): are entitled to a €10,000 annual exemption, valid for the entire period they maintain their cross-border status.
Both regimes imply that the gross income declared to the Swiss employer remains unchanged; the tax effect only applies on the Italian side of the declaration.
### Tax Rates in Switzerland
In Ticino, the source tax is determined by federal, cantonal, and municipal tariffs. As a dependent cross-border worker, you will automatically pay:
- AVS/AI/IPG (old-age, disability, unemployment): 5.3% of gross salary at the expense of the dependent - Accident insurance (AD/AC): 1.1% up to CHF 148,200 per year (maximum) - Malpractice insurance (LAMal): mandatory if you choose the Swiss system, with adult co-payments CHF 300–2,500 - LPP (complementary pension 2nd pillar): 7–18% depending on age (from 25 years)
All these amounts are deducted from the salary; the federal/cantonal source tax applies to the net pensionable income.
### Income Tax Declaration in Italy
Each cross-border worker must complete the model 730 at the Italian Revenue Agency by October 31 of each year, indicating in section CE the income produced in Switzerland and the Swiss tax credit. The amount certified by the Swiss employer (source tax certificate in Switzerland) serves to offset the Italian tax, avoiding double taxation. Use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to visualize the impact of Swiss withholdings and Italian exemption on your remuneration.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Practical Guide: Five Steps to Become a Frontalier
### Step 1: Employment Contract and Permit G
The first step is to sign an employment contract with an employer in Ticino. The employer will provide the necessary documentation to apply for the frontalier residence permit (Permit G) at the Questura of Como or the competent territorial prefecture, depending on the province of residence. The permit authorizes work in Switzerland as a resident frontalier in Italy and must be requested before the start of the employment relationship. On average, the permit G application process takes 30–60 days.
### Step 2: INPS Registration and Previdential Communications
Although the main contribution payments are made in Switzerland (through AVS), it is necessary to inform the INPS that you are a frontalier with foreign work. This avoids double contributions and allows the recognition of Swiss contributory periods for Italian pensions (if requested in the future). Contact your CAF reference at Como to deposit the frontaliership communication with Italian authorities.
### Step 3: Choice and Registration of Health Insurance
If you reside in Italy but work in Switzerland, you can opt for:
- **Swiss health insurance (LAMal)**: universal, with CHF 300–2,500 adult deductibles and variable monthly premiums per canton/insurer - Italian coverage (INPS/SSN): possible if you maintain Italian system registration
The choice must be communicated to the Swiss employer and competent authorities within the prescribed terms (usually within 30 days of starting work). It remains valid for a minimum period, usually 12 months.
### Step 4: Annual Tax Declaration
By October 31 of each year, the frontalier must submit the model 730 to the Revenue Agency (through CAF or autonomously online). Essential documents:
- Certified gross income from the Swiss employer (source tax certificate) - Withholding tax paid in Switzerland - Applicable exemption (€7,500 for old frontaliers, €10,000 for new ones) - Swiss credit for compensation

The first administrative step towards life as a cross-border commuter is obtaining the Permit G. Contrary to what many believe, the commuter does NOT apply for the permit directly: it is the Ticino-based employer who sends a formal authorization request to the SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) of Canton Ticino. Once SECO approves the request, the permit notification is sent to both the employer and the employee. Permit G is valid for 5 years and is easily renewable upon expiration if employment continues. It involves no costs for the employee and allows them to work legally in Ticino while residing in Italy (Cerano d'Intelvi or other municipalities in the Intelvi Valley).
### Tax return: calendar, forms, and annual procedure
Every year, the Italian cross-border commuter must submit their tax return to the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate). The deadline is November 30 for the income of the previous calendar year. In the tax return (model 730 or model Redditi PF), they must obligatorily indicate: - Gross employment income earned in Ticino - Withholding tax paid in Switzerland (documented by the year-end payslip extract) - Request for tax credit under Section CE (quadro CE)
The Revenue Agency processes the data, calculates the Italian personal income tax (IRPEF) by applying tax brackets and the tax credit, and applies the allowance provided for by the new agreement. If a refund is due, it is paid to the IBAN provided by the taxpayer within 4-6 months of processing the paperwork.
### AVS, LPP management and contribution monitoring
Old-age insurance (AVS) is mandatory from the very first day of work in Ticino. Annually, the commuter receives an AVS account statement from the competent cantonal body (Ahv-IV-Stelle Ticino) documenting the credited contributions. It is essential to keep these documents both for the Italian tax return and to verify proper contributions toward future pension benefits over time.
For the second pillar (LPP, mandatory occupational pension), the employer is required by law to register the employee with a pension fund within the first month of work. Switzerland is outside the European Union, so Swiss pension schemes (AVS, LPP) do not automatically coordinate with Italian ones (INPS): the commuter remains registered with the Italian INPS for contributions paid before moving to Ticino, while years of Swiss work accumulate in the AVS/LPP system.

## In Brief - G Permit to work as a border worker in Ticino, Switzerland; taxes withheld only in Switzerland - New Border Agreement from 2024: exemption of €10,000 income for new border workers - LAMal mandatory (CHF 300-2500/year), AVS 5.3% + Swiss social contributions - Double administration: tax declarations in Italy (730 quadro CE) and Switzerland
## Key Facts - **What**: Tax and contributory regime for border workers between Italy (Villa Guardia) and Switzerland (Ticino) - When: New Agreement from January 1, 2024 (signed on December 23, 2020, Law 83/2023) - Where: Border workers from the province of Varese towards Canton Ticino; border crossings: Brogeda, Gaggiolo, Chiasso - Who: Border workers with G Permit, Italian Revenue Agency, AFC/ESTV Switzerland, SECO - Contributions: AVS/AI 5.3%, AD 1.1%, LAMal CHF 300-2500/year, LPP 7-18%
### What it means to be a border worker from Villa Guardia Villa Guardia, an Italian town in the province of Varese, represents one of the many border towns from which daily workers move to work in Canton Ticino. Moving here (or staying) to work as a border worker in Switzerland involves tax, contributory, and administrative consequences that differ completely from the situation of a worker residing solely in Italy.
The main regime is summarized in a rule: the withholding tax on salaries and wages is withheld exclusively in Switzerland, never in Italy. This eliminates the risk of double taxation because Italy recognizes a tax credit through the model 730, quadro CE. The Convention on Double Taxation between Italy and Switzerland, signed on December 9, 1976, guarantees this bilateral system.
From January 1, 2024, the New Border Agreement (signed on December 23, 2020, and ratified in Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023) has introduced important innovations. For new border workers — those who acquire the status for the first time after July 17, 2023 — the exemption is set at €10,000 annual income, exempt from Italian taxation. Border workers who had already acquired the status before this date enjoy instead an exemption of €7,500, valid until 2033 (transitional regime).
### The Swiss-Italian tax system for border workers For a border worker from Villa Guardia working in Ticino, the annual tax cycle involves:
In Switzerland: The employer withholds the withholding tax directly from the paycheck. The percentage varies by canton and income, but is administered by the cantonal authorities (in Ticino, by the AFC/ESTV). At the end of the year, the border worker receives a certificate of the tax paid.
In Italy: The border worker declares the Swiss income through model 730 or Unico, specifying in the quadro CE the Swiss tax paid. This allows the border worker to claim the tax credit, which neutralizes the Italian IRPEF tax on the same taxable base. The Italian IRPEF tax rates (calculated on the Swiss gross income, without deduction of first-instance social contributions) are: 23% up to €28,000, 35% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000.
In practice: if the Swiss tax paid is lower than the Italian IRPEF tax, the border worker will have a credit (refund via 730). If higher, they generally will not owe anything in Italy because the credit covers the difference.
### Swiss social contributions and pension A border worker from Villa Guardia working as an employee in Ticino pays every month Swiss social contributions on their paycheck: AVS/AI (old-age, disability, survivors) at 5.3% at the employee's expense, AD (unemployment insurance) at 1.1% up to a maximum annual income of CHF 148,200, LAINF (accident insurance) from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector, and LPP (2nd pillar/pension fund) with a variable percentage for age ranges between 7% and 18%.
These contributions paid in Switzerland create pension rights in the Confederation, parallel to those INPS in Italy. The border worker accumulates, year after year, rights for the Swiss AVS pension and the LPP capital. With the [calculator](nav:calculator) available on the site, it is possible to simulate the impact of these contributions on the net monthly paycheck. ### Advantages and disadvantages of living in Villa Guardia as a border worker
Living in Villa Guardia and working in Ticino entails advantages and disadvantages that the potential border worker must carefully evaluate before moving or deciding to stay. The cost of living in the province of Varese is generally lower than in many areas of the Canton of Ticino, allowing a better quality of life with the same salary. Staying in Italy simplifies the management of the social, family and school network (children enrolled in Italian schools, general practitioner, municipal relations). A double health coverage (Italian INPS + Swiss LAMal) offers protection on two parallel systems. The administrative flexibility — maintaining Italian residence — facilitates relations with municipal offices, issuance of documents, registry registrations.
The negative sides include daily commuting to border crossings (Brogeda, Gaggiolo, Chiasso) with travel times linked to cross-border traffic flows. Dual administrative management requires tax returns in both countries with different calendars and deadlines to be carefully tracked. LAMal (Swiss health insurance) is mandatory with an excess of CHF 300-2500/year, additional to the Italian INPS. The currency exchange risk is concrete: salary in CHF, expenses at Villa Guardia in EUR; changes in the CHF/EUR rate affect real purchasing power. Finally, the renewal bureaucracy
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### What to Consider Before Relocating (or Staying) in Villa Guardia as a Border Worker #### Required Documentation and Request for the G Permit The procedure for obtaining the G Permit from Villa Guardia involves: obtaining a written employment contract from a Ticinese company (essential for the request), submitting a G Permit application to Swiss authorities (SECO/SEM) through the employer, registering with the Villa Guardia municipality as a resident if not already domiciled, and obtaining an Italian municipality certificate of residence to be submitted to Swiss authorities. Typically requested documentation: valid passport or ID card, signed employment contract, Italian certificate of residence, G Permit application form completed with the employer, confirmation of registration with the Italian municipality, and (if necessary) certificate of pending charges or judicial record. Processing times vary from 2 to 6 weeks. Once acquired, the permit is renewable as long as the employment relationship in Switzerland exists. #### Annual Fiscal Deadlines and Calendars A border worker from Villa Guardia must respect two parallel fiscal calendars. **In Italy**: The 730 or Unico model must be declared by May 31 (if submitted in person) or by June 30 (if submitted electronically); the CE form must be completed to claim the Swiss tax paid; the Agency's communication on refund or debt arrives by the end of the year. In Switzerland: The source tax is automatically withheld from the monthly paycheck; some cantons (including Ticino) require an annual income tax return — check with the cantonal administration of contributions (AFC/ESTV). The Italian deadline is critical: if the 730 (CE form) is not submitted within the deadline, the right to claim the tax credit is lost, compromising the fiscal advantage of border work. For support on deadlines and declarations, consult the tax-return guide available on the website. #### Managing LAMal: Deadlines and Renewal LAMal must be signed within 3 months of starting work in Switzerland. Annual renewal typically takes place between November and December for the following year. It is essential to respect these deadlines to avoid interruptions in coverage and administrative penalties. In addition, the border worker will need to pay the monthly or quarterly premium to the chosen private insurer (companies such as Helsana, CSS, Concordia, Sanitas are among the main ones in Ticino). #### Practical Tools and Support for the Border Worker The Frontaliere Ticino website provides concrete resources: a border worker salary calculator that simulates the net monthly income after AVS, Swiss social contributions, and source tax; a G Permit vs B Permit comparator to evaluate the pros and cons of the two options (Italian residence vs Swiss residence); a tax-return guide with deadlines, declarations, 730 model compilation, and CE form; detailed information on LAMal/CMI with franchises, insurers, and legal obligations. #### Long-Term Prospects: The Three Options Who lives in Villa Guardia and works in Ticino has three possible paths over time. Option 1 — Continue as a G Permit holder (permanent Italian residence): renew the G Permit annually, maintain residence in Villa Guardia, continue paying AVS/LPP in Switzerland. Advantages: administrative stability in Italy, lower costs. Disadvantages: continuous commuting, double bureaucratic management. Option 2 — Switch to a B Permit (Swiss residence): after 5+ years of border work, request a change of residence in Ticino and acquire a B Permit. Advantages: administrative simplification, full Swiss rights. Disadvantages: relocation, change in cantonal/comunal taxes, abandonment of Italian social network. Option 3 — Return to Italy full-time: cease work in Switzerland, return to the Italian fiscal/previdential regime, collect any accumulated LPP. Each choice has implications for future AVS income, LPP capital, Italian INPS rights, and residence in both countries. If you are evaluating a transfer to Villa Guardia as a border worker, start with the [calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate your net monthly income in Switzerland, then consult the tax-return guide to understand the declaration deadlines.

item.title: Living in San Fermo della Battaglia and working in Ticino
item.description: Practical guide for G border workers: how to move from San Fermo della Battaglia, tax regime 2024, G Permit, commuting costs, procedure checklist.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell
- Frontier G pay taxes only in Switzerland with an excess of €10,000 per year - New Frontier Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 - Cost of living in border Italy is lower than Ticino - Crossings and daily commuting are structural for border crossers
## Key facts
- **What**: Tax regime for G border workers (Swiss taxation + Italian tax credit) - When: From 1 January 2024 (New Agreement signed 23 December 2020) - Where: Ticino border areas (Chiasso, Brogeda, Mendrisio, Locarno) - Who: Employees with G Permit from Italy - Deductible: €10,000 per year for new frontier workers - Swiss taxes: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3%, AD/AC 1.1% - Italy tax: Avoided by tax credit (EC framework of 730)
Living in San Fermo della Battaglia and working in Ticino is one of the most frequent choices for those looking to combine quality of Italian life with Swiss salaries. The province of Como, a few kilometres from the Ticino border, makes this logistically viable option for thousands of border crossers.
The New Frontier Agreement, which entered into force on 1 January 2024, has transformed the tax regime significantly. New frontier workers benefit from a deductible of €10,000 per year. The crucial element: the tax at source is withheld exclusively in Switzerland. Italy recognizes tax credits to avoid double taxation through the CE framework of the model 730.
